tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much
tenebat: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, grasp (3rd sg. impf.)
tenet: teneō, tenēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, occupy (3rd sg. pres.)
terra: terra, -ae (f.) — land, earth, ground (nom./abl. sg.) · also f. voc. sg. (ō terra hospita)
testor: testor, -ārī, testātus sum — to call to witness, swear by (1st sg. pres., deponent)
teucri: Teucer, Teucrī (m.) — Teucer, early king of Troy (gen. sg.) · also Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) Trojans (voc. pl.: Teucrī, secludite) · also m. nom. pl. (Teucrī, Trojans)
thalamo: thalamus, -ī (m.) — bedchamber, inner room, bridal chamber (abl./dat. sg., Greek)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
totaque: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (f. abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
troia: Trōius, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (abl. sg., from Troy) · also nom. sg., Troy (servātaque serves Trōia fidem)
tuis: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (m./n. abl./dat. pl.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turbida: turbidus, -a, -um — stormy, turbulent, confused (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom. sg.)
tuta: tūtus, -a, -um — safe, sheltered (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
tyrii: Tyrius, -a, -um — Tyrian, of Tyre in Phoenicia; Carthaginian (m. nom. pl.) · also m. voc. pl. (Tyriī, celebrāte)
ubera: ūber, ūberis (n.) — udder, teat, breast (acc./nom. pl.)
umbra: umbra, -ae (f.) — shade, shadow (abl. sg.; nom. sg.)
undosum: undōsus, -a, -um — wavy, surging (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
utrumque: uterque, utraque, utrumque — each of two, both (n. acc. sg.: in utrumque, for either event)
velut: velut (adv.) — as, just as, as if
veniet: veniō, venīre, vēnī, ventum — to come (3rd sg. fut.)
vero: vērō (adv.) — in truth, indeed, but; tum vērō, then indeed
victis: vincō, vincere, vīcī, victum — to conquer (perf. pass. part., m./n. abl. pl.) · also dat. pl. (ūna salūs victīs)
victus: vincō, -ere, vīcī, victum — to conquer, overcome (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
vidi: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (1st sg. perf.)
volvens: volvō, volvere, volvī, volūtum — to roll, unroll, ponder (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
